name: CRT / Analog Video Effects
visualIdentity: Explicitly defined analog-display treatment: scanlines, mild color offsets, persistence, screen curvature, and restrained noise. Keep effects within the screen context, scale detail to output resolution, and preserve legible information.
suitableUses: Best for retro game trailers, nostalgic technology stories, in-world broadcasts, or clean imagery presented as an analog screen. Also suits explanatory, editorial, or cinematic content when the CRT treatment supports the subject. This suitability is inferred from the supplied examples.
limitations: The source explicitly requires restrained distortion, legibility, no persistent flashes, and no exaggerated noise. Avoid applying CRT to modern screens unless requested, blurred art, or surrounding set elements. Do not stack Glitch Art as another corruption layer. Short pieces may not need chapter transitions; omit disruptive motion when it obscures meaning or breaks continuous-shot or loop requirements.
palette: No canonical palette is specified. Preserve signal, task, brand, reference, and source-art colors exactly; transient RGB offsets are an effect, not permission to recolor. Optional fallback tokens for new presentation elements only: background #171C24, foreground #E9E5D8, accent #6A9DAA. Keep three discrete base colors, no gradient, and verify contrast in the composited scene.
motionAndInteraction: Use deterministic, screen-space postprocessing with controlled scanlines, persistence, offsets, and curvature. For video, evaluate from seekable composition time; support direct, backward, and out-of-order seeks. Optional scrambled reveals suit short titles only, with exact final copy and readable holds. Optional chapter/story progress can coordinate scenes; use bounded glitch cuts only for intentionally abrasive moments, with clean endpoints and reduced-motion cuts. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to reversible states, preserve readable static/reduced-motion states, and support keyboard or touch where applicable.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or sound layer is specified. Propose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the actual topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices, keep speech clear, and synchronize and mix in the export pipeline. Do not assume assets exist.
assetRequirements: Apply the effect to high-quality source imagery or content explicitly shown on a screen. For device scenes, keep processing on the screen surface. Video textures require aligned UVs, preloaded media, and composition-time synchronization; direct seeks may need decoded frames or a verified adapter. Seed noise and cache stateful work; preserve authorized footage, exact copy, and original asset colors.
combinations: Use CRT alone as a finishing pass over clean content in an analog context. Pixel art (style-057) can gain authentic raster presentation when rendered at native resolution, integer-upscaled, and treated with restrained scanlines and bleed. Pair with device/set style-065 only when it supplies an era-appropriate housing; restrict artifacts to its screen. These roles are explicit examples. Avoid a second corruption filter.
productionApproach: Separate responsibilities: WebGL/GLSL with Three.js may render the screen-space style; GSAP may own seekable motion; HyperFrames owns composition, timing, media/audio sync, validation, and export. Remotion is only a fallback for unavailability or a verified required limitation. Choose only needed tools; native Canvas/SVG may suffice. Inspect representative frames and the decoded video for readability, synchronization, dimensions, duration, frame rate, audio, and loop seams. For HTML interactions, keep live input out of video export and check reversal and reduced motion.
